Verified correct on test; initial incorrect answer came from misaligning lower-panel rows while hand-indexing.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T04:24:37.405230+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T04:24:37.405244+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_6d6b3311_move_motif_to_full_length_2_stripe_and_add_8_trail', kind='memory', title='ARC task-6d6b3311: move motif toward 2 divider, then add far-side 8 stripe', content='For Continual-ARC task-6d6b3311, find the full straight color-2 divider and the separate colored motif on one side. This validates moving the shape until adjacent even across a large gap, then placing 8 immediately on the far side.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T05:09:14.198544+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T05:15:31.728829+00:00', version=3), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_6d6b3311_extend_pattern_toward_2_marker_and_place_8_boundary', kind='memory', title='ARC task-6d6b3311: shift toward 2 and add far-side 8 stripe (gap nuance)', content="Newer directly observed demos refine the older rule below: if exactly one background row/column lies between motif and 2-line, leave motif in place and add the 8 line immediately beyond its far edge; if gap is larger, move to adjacency, then add 8 beyond it. Across demos, horizontal strokes include the upper/lower occupied rows (connect across the full marker x-bounds, even if a boundary row has only two markers) and any dense intermediate row with >=3 marker cells (connect between that row’s first/last marker). Vertical strokes similarly occur on selected columns containing markers beyond just horizontal-stroke intersections, and fill gaps between/top-bottom stroke extent; avoid treating every repeated column as a line. Example decisive test: 8x29 background6, markers9; output changed only rows 2,5,7, filling gaps with 2 between 9s (row2 and row7 boundary strokes; row5 dense intermediate stroke), while rows3,4,6 stayed unchanged. Earlier overbroad hypotheses (fill every row/column span or extend all columns with >=3 markers) were incorrect. Useful demos: demos 1/2 had vertical 2 strokes through selected columns; demo3 showed columns with markers only on horizontal strokes are not necessarily vertical lines. Fill horizontal boundary spans between global stroke x-bounds c3..c9, so add 2 at r2c3 and r11c8. Extend the c3 vertical stroke from the top boundary r2 through bottom boundary r11 (the top extension links it into the upper horizontal stroke); fill its gaps r3,r5,r7,r10. Fill c9 gaps r3,r10 over r2..r11. The correct output changed exactly these cells: (r2,c3),(r3,c3),(r3,c9),(r5,c3),(r7,c3),(r10,c3),(r10,c9),(r11,c8), all to 2. Two failed attempts omitted r3c3 because the left vertical stroke begins below the top horizontal row; it must connect up to the top boundary after that row's horizontal span reaches the column. Demo 3 also confirms top boundary horizontal can extend across global x-bounds to reach a vertical stroke, while ordinary interior horizontal fills occur only between their row markers. Use the whole connected stroke system, not just gaps directly between same-row markers.

Confirmed fresh test (18x12, background 7, markers 9): marker rows r8 and r13 were the horizontal boundary strokes, with overall stroke columns c3..c11. On r8, fill c4 and c9-c10; on r13, fill c4-c6 and c8, extending those horizontal strokes across c3..c11. The selected vertical side strokes were c3 and c11, because each had marker evidence on the boundary plus an additional interior marker: c3 markers at r8,r10,r13; c11 at r8,r13 (with r12c11 marker). Fill vertical gaps c3 at r9,r11,r12, and c11 at r9-r11. Exact changed cells: (r8,c4),(r8,c9),(r8,c10),(r9,c3),(r9,c11),(r10,c11),(r11,c3),(r11,c11),(r12,c3),(r13,c4),(r13,c5),(r13,c6),(r13,c8), all to 2. Other repeated marker column c12 is not a vertical stroke: it appears on boundary rows and dense interior row only. This directly confirms the selection principle: interior markers away from horizontal stroke rows select a vertical, while boundary/dense-row intersections alone do not.", path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T04:39:30.889917+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T04:56:07.224508+00:00', version=4)]
